note: Curated Vermont solar / net-metering / regulatory updates for array operators. Refreshed by a scheduled research agent; verify against the linked source before relying on any figure.

items.title: New net-metering rates take effect August 1
items.summary: The Category I effective credit falls about 2¢ to ≈ $0.1439/kWh as the small-solar siting charge rises 4¢ → 5¢/kWh. Applies to systems permitted on or after Aug 1, 2026; existing arrays keep their locked rate.

items.title: Op-ed: Vermont's net-metering decision just made solar harder
items.summary: VTDigger commentary on the PUC's 2026 biennial cut and what a 7th straight reduction to the Category I adjustor means for solar economics in the state.

items.title: PUC issues 2026 biennial net-metering update — Case 26-0291-INV
items.summary: The Commission's statutorily required order adjusting net-metering compensation. It raised the siting charge for small solar to 5¢/kWh for permits filed Aug 1, 2026 – Jul 31, 2028.

items.title: DPS urges a wholesale net-metering rulemaking instead of another formula tweak
items.summary: The Department of Public Service recommended the Commission open a broader rulemaking to reform net metering — a signal that larger structural changes to compensation could be coming.

items.title: Over 1,000 Vermonters comment against further net-metering cuts
items.summary: Public pushback on the biennial update as installations have fallen ~32% since 2017 across seven consecutive compensation reductions.

items.title: H.289 overhauls the RES and phases out community / offsite net metering
items.summary: Vermont's Renewable Energy Standard rewrite raises renewables to 100% by 2030 and ends new offsite ('virtual') group net metering starting Jan 2025, with a mandated study of a successor program. Existing group systems continue.
